guide.title: Mission Bay, San Francisco: Chase Center, the UCSF campus and the Third Street Bridge
guide.intro: Mission Bay is the San Francisco district that runs from Mission Creek Channel south to Mariposa Street, with San Francisco Bay along its eastern edge. Chase Center stands at 1 Warriors Way, and the arena's own site gives its opening as 2019 and names it the home of the Golden State Warriors and the Golden State Valkyries, with the surrounding district called Thrive City. The UCSF Mission Bay campus occupies blocks addressed on Owens Street, Illinois Street, Gene Friend Way, Nelson Rising Lane, 16th Street and Third Street. Third Street crosses Mission Creek Channel on the Third Street Bridge, also called the Lefty O'Doul Bridge, which is San Francisco Landmark No. 194, designated in 1989. The Garcia and Maggini Warehouse stands at 128 King Street and is San Francisco Landmark No. 229, designated in 2002.

sections.heading: Chase Center and Thrive City
sections.body:
Chase Center is the arena at 1 Warriors Way, San Francisco, CA 94158. Its own site describes it as a sports and entertainment arena in San Francisco's Mission Bay neighbourhood, gives its opening as 2019, and names it the home of the Golden State Warriors and the Golden State Valkyries. The site also names the district around the arena Thrive City.

No source states general opening hours or ticket prices for the arena, so none are given here; the schedule is by event.

The Muni Metro T Third Street line serves the arena. Its stop list carries UCSF/Chase Center and UCSF/Chase Center (16th St).

sections.heading: The UCSF Mission Bay campus
sections.body:
UCSF describes Mission Bay as a teaching, research and clinical care campus with a daily population of about 3,500 faculty, staff, students, patients and other visitors, more than one million square feet of research space, and an integrated hospital that serves women, children and cancer patients.

The campus covers several blocks and its departments carry separate street addresses. City business records place UCSF departments on Owens Street, Illinois Street, Gene Friend Way, Nelson Rising Lane, 16th Street, Third Street and Berry Street.

No source states visitor hours or a public entrance for the campus, so none are given here.

sections.heading: Mission Creek, the parks and the houseboats
sections.body:
Mission Creek Park runs along the channel at 290 Channel Street. San Francisco Recreation and Park holds it as a neighbourhood park and records it at 17.2 acres.

Houseboats are moored on the creek along Channel Street. San Francisco's register of business locations records the Mission Creek Harbor Association at 300 Channel Street, with a registration date of 22 December 1978. No source states visiting arrangements or a berth address for the moorings, so none are given here.

Recreation and Park also holds Mission Bay Park, recorded at 11.6 acres in the 94158 ZIP code, and Mariposa Park, recorded at 2.7 acres on the Mariposa Street line.

sections.heading: The Third Street Bridge and the Garcia and Maggini Warehouse
sections.body:
The Third Street Bridge carries Third Street over Mission Creek Channel and is also called the Lefty O'Doul Bridge. It is San Francisco Landmark No. 194, designated in 1989. The Strauss Engineering Corporation designed the bascule span, which opened in 1933; the earlier crossing on the site closed to traffic in 1931. The main span is a 143-foot single-leaf bascule truss over a 104-foot channel, and the Operator's and Watchman's Houses stand on the piers.

The Garcia and Maggini Warehouse stands at 128 King Street. It is San Francisco Landmark No. 229, designated in 2002.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
The Muni Metro T Third Street line runs up Third Street through the district, and its stops here are UCSF/Chase Center and UCSF/Chase Center (16th St). Northbound, the line leaves Third Street at Channel Street and runs by way of Fourth Street into the Central Subway.

By street: Chase Center is at 1 Warriors Way, 94158. Mission Creek Park is at 290 Channel Street, 94158. The Garcia and Maggini Warehouse is at 128 King Street. The Third Street Bridge carries Third Street over Mission Creek Channel.

Mariposa Street is the line between Mission Bay and Dogpatch, and Dogpatch runs south from that street to Cesar Chavez Street.

faq.question: Which buildings and structures in Mission Bay carry a designation, and what are the numbers?
faq.answer: The Third Street Bridge, which carries Third Street over Mission Creek Channel and is also called the Lefty O'Doul Bridge, is San Francisco Landmark No. 194, designated in 1989. The Garcia and Maggini Warehouse at 128 King Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 229, designated in 2002.

faq.question: Where is Chase Center and when did it open?
faq.answer: Chase Center is at 1 Warriors Way, San Francisco, CA 94158. The arena's own site gives its opening as 2019 and names it the home of the Golden State Warriors and the Golden State Valkyries, with the surrounding district called Thrive City. faq.question: How do I reach Mission Bay on Muni?
faq.answer: The Muni Metro T Third Street line runs up Third Street through the district, and its stops here are UCSF/Chase Center and UCSF/Chase Center (16th St). Northbound, the line leaves Third Street at Channel Street and runs by way of Fourth Street into the Central Subway.

faq.question: Can I walk along Mission Creek and see the houseboats?
faq.answer: Mission Creek Park runs along the channel at 290 Channel Street, and San Francisco Recreation and Park holds it as a neighbourhood park of 17.2 acres. The houseboats are moored on the creek along the same street. No source states visiting arrangements or a berth address for the moorings, so none are given here.

faq.question: Where does Mission Bay stop and Dogpatch begin?
faq.answer: Mariposa Street is the line between them, and the city's neighbourhood polygons put Mission Bay's southern edge on that street. Dogpatch runs south from Mariposa Street to Cesar Chavez Street and holds the Pier 70 yard, the Museum of Craft and Design, the Minnesota Street Project and Esprit Park.
